newsitem.title: EGYPT: PRESS DIGEST - Egypt economic press - May 25.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Egypt economic press - May 25.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the Egyptian economic press this week. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
AL-BORSA
- Oriental Weavers offer to increase capital opens today. Offer is the biggest by a private company.
- Head of Capital Market Authority, Abdel Hamid Ibrahim, says the forged stocks matter is a minor problem and the authority has taken three steps to prevent it from recurring.

- Suez Canal Bank board approves raising the bank's capital to 100 million pounds ($29.6 million) from 50 million pounds. Financial Director Adel Sanhouri says the issue will be raised at the annual general meeting on June 31 for final approval.
- Bourse activity declines in April.
- Discount rate falls for the fourth time in seven months.
- Industrial Development Bank 150 million pound bond offer closes fully subscribed.

- Eipico/Egyptian International Pharmaceutical Industries net after-tax profits for the first three months of the 1996/7 financial year rose to 17.0 million pounds from 15.5 million in the same period of the previous year. Sales were higher at 83 million in 96/7 compared to 71 million. The year begins on July 1.

- Medinet Nasr Housing and Development made net after-tax profits for the first nine-months of the 1996/7 financial year of 156.37 million, including 70.168 million from selling its shares in Heliopolis Housing and Development . The company made net after-tax profits of 78.75 million for the same period of 1995/6.

- Delta International Bank has improved net pre-tax profits for the first three months of 1997 to 11.553 million from 5.753 million in the same period of the previous year. The increase is mainly due to more customer deposits.
- State offers a minimum 10 percent in Kabo/Nasr Clothing and Textiles.
- Egyptian Electro Cables net pre-tax profit falls to 15.2 million pounds for the first nine-months of 1996/7 compared to 20.5 million in the same year ago period.
- Commercial International Bank 300 million pound bond offer closed 1.57 times oversubscribed.
- National Societe Generale Bank may issue bonds for 150 million in June.
- Misr Free Shops MSFC.CA, Development and Engineering Consultancy hold extraordinary annual general meeting to change status to private holding from public holding and elect new board.
- A relative stabilisation comes after the sharp rise in prices.

- Al-Ahram Beverages (Pyramids Breweries) expects net sales to rise to 166.8 million for 1996/7 from 140.59 million in the previous year. Net profits for 96/7 will also be higher at 58 million compared to 44.87 million.
$ 1 = 3.395 pounds
